messages:
ana: FYI onboarding mobile QA hit a nasty SSE edge: when traffic goes through our edge proxy (CloudFront+shielding) + flaky cellular, fragments sometimes arrive out-of-order or coalesced and the mobile SDKs display duplicated mid-stream tokens.

ben: Oof. Is that the case where the gateway buffers small chunks and then sends them as one big chunk after a 504 retry?

ana: (typo) ana: yes — reproduced: 1) start Android sample app stream on a slow cellular emulator, 2) force a gateway 504 by stalling upstream for ~700ms, 3) resume connection. Result: client sees final "[DONE]"-like fragment before a few earlier partial fragments; sometimes a partial token is stitched onto the next message.

chloe: Interesting. Do we think it's strictly an edge buffering/coalescing problem or also parser/delimiting in the SDK?

ben: From packet traces: the edge coalesces chunked frames into a merged TCP segment when it retries; the server had emitted chunk A then B then resume token. The merged segment sometimes arrives after a reconnect in a different order due to reordering in the proxy retry path.

chloe: Android SDK uses a stateful delimiter parser that assumes arrival order; Go SDK is slightly more tolerant because it treats each newline as its own event. Mobile JS (React Native) forks the Node parsing and is brittle.

ana: (again!) ana: Minimal repro curl for infra folks (run behind simulated proxy):
```
# simulate slow upstream then allow retry
nc -l 8080 < server-stream.txt
# client
echo -e "GET /stream HTTP/1.1\r\nAuthorization: Bearer $TOKEN\r\n\r\n" | nc localhost 8080
```

edge-bot: Edge alert: observed 221 coalesced-chunk events in last 24h for /v1/stream in us-west. Proxy config: response_buffering=on, idle_timeout=600ms.

ben: Quick mitigations: 1) onboarding docs: call out proxy buffering and recommend response_buffering=off or chunked flush headers; 2) mobile sample: add a reconnect backoff + dedupe step; 3) server: include per-chunk monotonic seq-id in meta so clients can reorder/dedupe.

chloe: Agreed. Long-term: enhance SDK parsers to accept out-of-order fragments if seq-id present and to queue/reorder. Also add a parity test matrix: Android vs iOS vs ReactNative vs Go under simulated proxy reordering/timeouts.

ana: Filed internal issue & added to onboarding checklist: https://redwood.internal/issue/RED-4201. I'll push a tiny sample-app patch that toggles proxy buffering and shows a dedupe helper.

ci-bot: CI run 6120 attached: https://ci.redwood.ai/build/6120 (mobile-streaming-parity)

ben: Nice. One more ask: add a short blurb in the quickstart about "proxy settings to avoid chunk coalescing" so infrequent devs don't hit this during first-run. :thumbsup:
